blocks.text: World Food Day, observed every Oct. 16 by the United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), is meant to draw attention to the goal of eliminating hunger and ensuring access to safe, nutritious and sufficient food for all. In the Philippines, however, World Food Day 2026 presents a troubling paradox. While government agencies, local government units, schools and private organizations hold ceremonies, feeding programs, poster-making contests and other activities, millions of Filipinos continue to experience hunger, food insecurity, high food prices, declining farm productivity and climate-induced agricultural losses.
